visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: What does an internal wall at a bank stop?

options.text: The bank's stake in the outcome

questions.explain: A wall controls what people know, but it doesn't change what the bank stands to gain. That's why Goldman's wall didn't settle the conflict at El Paso.
questions.explain_at: A wall stops information. It does nothing about incentive

questions.q: A seller's bank earns 1% of the price, and the price rises by €100m. How much more does the bank earn?
questions.explain: 1% of €100m is €1m. On a €1bn sale, getting the deal done at all is worth €10m to the bank, ten times as much.
questions.explain_at: That last hundred million is worth one hundred million to the client

questions.q: A bank earns 1% for advising on a €1bn sale, and 2% for arranging €600m of debt for the winning bidder. What's its total fee?
questions.explain: €10m for the advice plus €12m for the debt. The financing fee is bigger than the advisory fee, which is why the bidder using the bank's debt matters to the bank.
questions.explain_at: So add it up: ten million for advice and twelve for the debt

questions.q: What does a fairness opinion say about the price?

options.text: It's financially fair, within a range
Shareholders should vote to accept it

questions.explain: It says the price is fair from a financial point of view, within a range, at a date. It doesn't call it the best price or tell shareholders how to vote.
questions.explain_at: A fairness opinion says the price is fair from a financial point of view

questions.q: Theramex's reported value went from about €1.2bn to about €2.6bn. What can you conclude about the sellers' return?

options.text: They made about 2.2 times their money
They made a profit of about €1.4bn
It depends on equity and debt we can't see
They earned about 20% a year on it

questions.explain: The reported figures value the whole company. The sellers' return depends on the equity they put in and the debt ahead of it, and neither is public.
questions.explain_at: it values the company, while their return depends on their equity
